attribution_limitations: Source conflict: the text says no IL-10 was detected, while Table 1 and Supplementary Table S1 print IL-10 at 0.39 FPKM. Both article sides are review-only; the Table S1 IL10 row should also be review-only.
Coding mutation counts: 7 insertions + 72 synonymous + 156 missense = 235, but 239 coding mutations are stated. Arithmetic-only mismatch; categories may be incomplete.

Duration of vemurafenib treatment at the follow-up sample is given as 2 years of intermittent treatment in one place and 21 months in another (December 2013 to 09/2015). Intermittent use and exact stop/start dates are not described. The 2-year wording is treated as a rounding of the dated 21 months; the 2-year fact is review-only.

Duration of the complete response: 31 months stated in the discussion, while the patient remained stable from December 2013 to December 2016 (about 36 months) in the case description. Dates are stated but the stability period and response duration may measure different intervals.

Source conflict on sample and pattern timing: the Figure 1 caption and the supplementary methods place PBMC-POST-1 at 6 months and POST-2 at 12 months, while Supplementary Figure 3 places PBMC-POST-1 at 12 months and the Results describe pattern 2 clones as detected at 12 months. Pattern 3 is placed at 48 months in one paragraph but at 24 months by the end of immunization in the next, and at POST-3 in the Figure 3D caption.

TQ-TIL pattern 1 is given as 31.6% of TQ-TIL clones, while the next sentence says 58% of TQ-TIL clones corresponded to pattern 1 clones expanded in blood at least three times. The source does not reconcile these.

Text fold changes 3-fold and 2-fold are rounded relative to the ratios 3.04 and 2.25 printed inside the Figure 2B image (10 matches). Image values are pixel content in visual.json only; the CD4 and CD20 text facts are review-only.

The abstract states that prevalent TIL clones (50%) were both new and preexisting and expanded in blood; the body reports 29.5% of TIL clones and 51% of TQ-TIL clones with these patterns. Not recorded as a fact.
The statement of increased serum IgG antibodies is attributed to earlier work and may describe a cohort rather than this patient.

Supplementary Table S1 prints different FPKM values for two genes that are also in main Table 1: CXCL1 24.48 in Table 1 versus 0.45 in Table S1, and CTLA4 1.82 in Table 1 versus 1.71 in Table S1. Other genes in both tables agree. Both sides are review-only.

Table 1 labels are printed with irregularities (for example LSGAL9 for galectin 9, Vimentine, trailing parentheses such as (PD-1) and (CTLA4) attached to ligand names); transcript names are kept as printed.

Cumulative frequencies of TIL clones in blood are given in the text as 5%, 10.7% and 8.9%, while the Figure 3F image prints 5.01%, 10.71% and 8.91%. Rounding only; image values stay in visual.json and the text facts are review-only.
